mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand and earnings pressure, which reduces corporate profit growth and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 6.5% and remains above for at least two months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods when UNRATE > 6.5% for two months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) for two consecutive quarters signals deteriorating demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of two consecutive quarterly GDPC1 declines (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.5% and remains above for at least three months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for three months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 140,000 for three consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS crosses above 140,000 and remains above for at least three months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods when PAYEMS > 140,000 for three months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) for two consecutive quarters signals strengthening demand, which boosts corporate revenue growth and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 rises for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of two consecutive quarterly GDPC1 rises (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months combined with a decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS) below 140,000 for three consecutive months signals severe labor market weakness, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 6.5% and remains above for at least two months AND PAYEMS crosses below 140,000 and remains below for at least three months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods when UNRATE > 6.5% for two months and PAYEMS < 140,000 for three months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) for two consecutive quarters combined with a decline in the Housing Index (HOUST) below 1,000 for three consecutive months signals strengthening demand but weakening housing demand, which boosts corporate revenue growth but reduces housing sector equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 rises for two consecutive quarters AND HOUST crosses below 1,000 and remains below for at least three months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods when GDPC1 rises for two quarters and HOUST < 1,000 for three months (t-test p > 0.05).
